title.value: SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021
title.justification: The title explicitly states the focus of the paper on the systematic review and meta-analysis of seroprevalence studies related to SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa within the specified time frame.
title.quote: SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021

analysis.description: This paper conducts a systematic review and meta-analysis of seroprevalence studies to estimate the exposure to SARS-CoV-2 in Africa from January 2020 to December 2021, informing public health measures and vaccine strategies.

type.justification: The paper is based on the synthesis and analysis of data from multiple seroprevalence studies, which is a hallmark of empirical research.
type.quote: We undertook a meta-analysis of population-based seroprevalence studies to estimate SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence in Africa to inform evidence-based decision making on public health and social measures (PHSM) and vaccine strategy.

name.justification: The research focuses on understanding the extent of SARS-CoV-2 spread through seroprevalence, a common epidemiological measure.
name.quote: We undertook a meta-analysis of population-based seroprevalence studies to estimate SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence in Africa.

name.justification: The study informs evidence-based decision making on public health measures across Africa, a clear aspect of Global Health.
name.quote: ...to inform evidence-based decision making on public health and social measures (PHSM) and vaccine strategy.
